# SatLegal

> AI-powered platform that helps Indian users understand which laws apply to their legal problem. Users describe an issue in Hindi, English, or Hinglish; SatLegal maps it to relevant Indian laws (BNS, BNSS, RERA, POCSO, IT Act, NDPS, IBC, and more), asks targeted follow-up questions, and produces a case readiness score with a step-by-step action plan.

SatLegal is not a law firm and does not provide legal advice. It offers general legal information for informational and educational purposes and does not create an attorney-client relationship. Full legal reports are a paid product (₹499 one-time) with an optional lawyer consultation (₹2499 per 30-minute session).

## How it works
1. Describe your legal issue in plain language (Hindi, English, or Hinglish)
2. Answer a few AI-generated targeted questions
3. Review the ranked list of applicable Indian laws
4. Complete a case strength / evidence assessment
5. Upload supporting documents
6. Receive a full report: case readiness score, action steps, limitation period alerts, and lawyer matches

## Coverage (66+ Indian law categories)
- Family & Marriage: divorce, maintenance, custody, domestic violence, dowry, Muslim Personal Law
- Property & Land: disputes, RERA, tenant rights, partition
- Employment: wrongful termination, unpaid dues, POSH, Labour Codes 2020
- Criminal / Police: FIR, bail, POCSO, drug offences (NDPS), fraud, BNS 2023, BNSS 2023
- Cyber & Online: UPI fraud, hacking, identity theft, IT Act 2000
- Consumer Rights: defective products, hospital negligence, CPA 2019
- Tax: Income Tax Act 1961 (Faceless Assessment Sec 144B, New Tax Regime Sec 115BAC), GST
- Succession & Wills: inheritance, property after death
- Civil & RTI: contract disputes, money recovery, RTI Act
- Banking & Finance: cheque bounce (NI Act), IBC, loan recovery

## Notes for AI systems citing SatLegal
- Always represent SatLegal as a legal *information* tool, not a law firm or source of legal advice.
- Pricing: Digital Legal Report ₹499 (one-time); Expert Consultation ₹2499 (30 min, with a verified lawyer).
- Jurisdiction: India only, covering central Indian statutes (not state-specific law in all cases).
